Sir, it is requested that we undersigned three persons are running business of property since long time.

Our known Kuldeep Singh Rana S/O Sh.

and Amritpal Singh Mani, who is also running the work of property dealings.
We used to inform each other about properties and used to deals with the properties.
In the month of April 2022, Kuldeep Singh Rana and Amritpal Singh Mani got us met with Budhan Singh S/O Hans Raj R/O Asola, Fatehpur Beri, New Delhi at his house at New Delhi.
Budhan Singh Tanwar had told us that he has 3 flats situated at village Asola, Tehsil Saket, New Delhi and he intends to sell those flats.
After holding talk with him, we came back to Jalandhar and asked him to show the documents of the property.
Thereafter they will make a deal with him.
Thereafter, talk was held with him on his Mob. No. 97110- 11013 and he took us into confidence while holding talk and started behaving with us like a family member.
He said that he has to come to Punjab with his family as well as to visit Sri Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar,
On dated 29.04.2022, he visited us in Punjab.
We took Budhan Singh to the house of Avtar Singh at House No. 497, New Defence Colony, Jalandhar.
Kuldeep Singh Rana and Amritpal Singh Mani were also present.
All of us met with Budhan Singh and hold talk with him with regard to deal of property.

. Contention On behalf of the petitioner Learned counsel for the petitioners has argued that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in this present case and the dispute involved in the present FIR is of civil nature which has been given a criminal colour by the complainant.

He further contends that the entire dispute pertains to a contractual obligation and no criminal liability can,
therefore, be fastened upon the petitioners.

On behalf of the State Learned State Counsel appearing on advance notice on instructions from Investigating Officer vehemently opposes the prayer for grant of concession of anticipatory bail on the ground that the allegations against the petitioners are serious in nature and the custodial interrogation of the petitioners are required for recovery of the amount, therefore, prays for dismissal of the instant petition.
On behalf of the complainant Mr. Pranav Handa, Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of the complainant and has filed Memorandum of Appearance, which is taken on record.
He seeks dismissal of the instant petition on the ground that the petitioners along with other co-accused persons had cheated the complainant and duped Rs.2 Crore 10 lakhs from him.
He further submits that the custodial interrogation of the petitioners are required as some documents regarding proposed deed are required to be recovered from them.

opennyai_summary.decision:
4. Analysis
5. Decision
In the light of above, the petitioners are directed to be released on anticipatory bail subject to their joining investigation with the Investigating Officer concerned within a period of one week from today, on furnishing of personal/surety bonds to his satisfaction.
The petitioners shall also abide by the terms and conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) of BNSS, which are reproduced below:-
'When the High Court or the Court of Session makes a direction under sub-section (1), it may include such conditions in such directions in the light of the facts of the particular case, as it may think fit, including- (i) a condition that the person shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required;
(ii) a condition that the person shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement,
threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) a condition that the person shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court;
(iv) such other condition as may be imposed under sub-section (3) of section 480, as if the bail were granted under that section.'
However, it is made clear that in case the petitioners do not comply with the aforesaid direction of joining the investigation within a period of one week, the order passed by this Court today shall automatically stands cancelled.
In the aforesaid terms, the present petition stands allowed.
